scope: Final visible draft, deployed JSON parity, exact source/article/action bytes, October 29 review-correction-acceptance train identities and timing, consumed held-action grant receipt, CI scope enforcement, open fleet PR arithmetic, pre-generation PR reviews and dispositions, byte-budget arithmetic, and current review discovery. Read-only review; no article revision or acceptance, finding disposition, action admission or settlement, readiness, merge, workflow dispatch, runtime, or scheduling authority.

findings.title: PR 505 is Codex review data, not a Claude invocation
findings.location: Line 17 calls PR #505 a separate Claude invocation with a bounded evidence view that returned a structured verdict.
findings.explanation: PR #505 publishes the Codex independent-daily-article-review record and changes only the full review, registered JSON and review registry. Its exact-source handoff identifies Codex and says no exact reviewer model configuration was exposed. No Claude provider invocation or receipt is part of that PR.
findings.correction: Identify #505 as the source-pinned Codex article review, distinct from the native Sonnet/Opus action-review path and from GitHub transport identity.

findings.title: The October 28 one-use grant was already consumed
findings.location: Lines 72, 96 and 97 say grant #506 is ready for a guarded dispatch and is the immediate available next action.
findings.explanation: Before article generation, run 41089029461 had already reserved and consumed the grant and operation from PR #506. It stopped held-invalid-output before Opus, produced no proposal, and the receipt explicitly says no rerun is authorized.
findings.correction: Report the consumed attempt and its typed failure. Preserve the candidates as Needs Review, but do not recommend dispatching #506 or present /dispatch-action as executable.

findings.title: The acceptance PR is given the source-pin merge time
findings.location: Line 72 says PR #512 accepted the article at 20:57Z Friday.
findings.explanation: PR #512 merged at 20:48:12Z as eea50cff. PR #513, the accepted-source review, merged at 20:57:08Z as a82f7dd7.
findings.correction: Use 20:48:12Z for acceptance and 20:57:08Z for the later source-pinned review.

findings.title: The claimed generic workflow-stage CI gate does not exist
findings.location: Line 66 says CI rejects PRs that touch more than one workflow stage.
findings.explanation: The PR Check workflow runs browser, type, lint, unit, article-reference and pipeline checks plus branch-specific acceptance validation. Editorial helpers guard exact paths for accept operations, but no check classifies arbitrary changed files by workflow stage or rejects a PR for spanning stages.
findings.correction: Say the train used scoped PRs and branch-specific path guards. Do not claim a repository-wide semantic stage-scope CI rule.

findings.title: The open fleet PR total is fourteen, not thirteen
findings.location: Line 76 reports thirteen open PRs, while lines 78 through 86 enumerate seven plus one plus two plus one plus three.
findings.explanation: The listed counts total 14. The primary PR records named by the article were open at the source snapshot.
findings.correction: Report fourteen open PRs across five repos, or state a specific exclusion rule and adjust the itemized list.

findings.title: Workstation 8 through 10 already had substantive reviews
findings.location: Lines 78 and 99 say no findings were posted on any Workstation PR #4 through #10.
findings.explanation: Before generator run #281 began, PR #8 had a detailed replace review, PR #9 had three reviews, and PR #10 had a replace review. They include test receipts, ranked findings, and explicit replacement or deletion recommendations.
findings.correction: Keep #4 through #7 as having no posted findings, but report the actual pre-reviews and dispositions on #8 through #10.

findings.title: Classic Space 4 has explicit blockers and a checkpoint
findings.location: Lines 82, 96 and 100 say no blocker or holding reason is recorded for Classic Space Venue #4.
findings.explanation: The October 27 review requires two fixes: narrow the animation-export conclusion and add source identities to the depth ledger. It names a revised research head as the next checkpoint, the PR author as correction owner, and James as merge and dispatcher authority.
findings.correction: Report the two requested corrections, revised-head checkpoint, and owner and merge gates instead of asking for a new blocker name or closure.

findings.title: LEGO 44 and 46 have recorded dispositions and owners
findings.location: Lines 86, 96 and 102 say DO NOT MERGE is only a warning and no disposition is recorded for #44 or #46.
findings.explanation: PR #44 explicitly preserves a non-operative analysis snapshot and makes no import or register change. PR #46 is a reviewed derivative with four named follow-up owner roles, reviewer and acceptance requirements, James's retained authority, an exact pickup source, and exit criteria.
findings.correction: Describe #44 as a preserved non-operative review snapshot and #46 as a reviewed derivative with named follow-up owners and exit criteria.

findings.title: The 320 KiB budget percentage uses a decimal denominator
findings.location: Lines 74 and 98 say 274,352 bytes consume 86 percent of a 320 KiB budget.
findings.explanation: 320 KiB is 327,680 bytes, so 274,352 bytes is about 83.73 percent. The 86 percent figure follows only if 320 KiB is incorrectly treated as 320,000 bytes.
findings.correction: Report approximately 83.7 percent, or explicitly use a decimal 320,000-byte limit. Keep byte budgets distinct from tokenizer or provider counts.
